summary: "Google has transferred its Agent2Agent Protocol to the newly formed Agentic AI Foundation, signaling a push for standardization in multi-agent AI systems across the industry."

Google announced the transfer of its Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A) to the newly established Agentic AI Foundation, marking a significant step toward industry-wide standardization of multi-agent AI communication. The move represents one of the most substantial open-standards initiatives in the AI agent space to date.

The Agent2Agent Protocol, first introduced by Google earlier this year, enables AI agents to communicate, coordinate, and collaborate across different platforms and providers. By placing the protocol under an independent foundation, Google aims to prevent vendor lock-in and encourage broader adoption across the AI industry.

The Agentic AI Foundation will govern the protocol's development, maintain technical specifications, and oversee certification processes for implementations. Founding members include Google, Anthropic, Microsoft, and several other major AI labs—a coalition that signals unusual industry consensus on the need for standardization.

Multi-agent AI systems represent the next frontier in artificial intelligence development. Unlike single-model deployments, agentic systems require sophisticated coordination protocols to manage task delegation, context sharing, and outcome reconciliation across multiple specialized agents. The absence of standard protocols has created fragmented ecosystems where agents from different providers often cannot interoperate effectively.

Industry analysts note that Google's decision to open the protocol through a foundation model mirrors earlier standardization efforts in other technology domains. The success of protocols like HTTP and TCP enabled the modern internet; similarly, A2A supporters argue that standardized agent communication could unlock the full potential of enterprise AI deployments.

The foundation structure addresses concerns about vendor neutrality. Unlike protocols controlled by single companies, the Agentic AI Foundation will manage A2A through a governance model that gives member organizations—regardless of size—input into technical direction and specification updates.

Enterprise adoption of AI agents has accelerated rapidly in 2026, with major deployments requiring agents to work across cloud providers, model providers, and internal systems. The lack of standardization has been cited as a primary barrier to more widespread agent deployments in regulated industries and large enterprises.

Technical specifications for A2A are available through the foundation's website, with reference implementations in Python and JavaScript already released. The foundation has indicated that compliance testing and certification programs will be available by Q4 2026.
